definition: a piece of kitchen equipment that you use to cook food or heat things

collocations.example: We cook all our meals on a gas stove.
Please turn off the stove before you leave home.

definition: describing an animal that has no home or has wandered away from one

collocations.example: A stray dog followed us all the way home.
The shelter takes in stray animals from the streets.

definition: to try very hard to achieve or obtain something

collocations.example: We strive for excellence in everything our company does.
You should always strive to achieve your personal goals.

definition: determined not to change your opinion or way of doing things

collocations.example: He is too stubborn to admit he was wrong.
She has a stubborn streak and rarely backs down.

definition: a metal pin or bolt used to fasten or support parts together

collocations.example: The engineer tightened each stud bolt on the flange.
They fixed the heavy shelf to a wooden wall stud.

definition: the short part of a tree trunk left in the ground after it is cut down

collocations.example: We sat down to rest on a tree stump.
A rotting stump remained where the old oak stood.

definition: a ship that can travel under the surface of the sea

collocations.example: The navy launched a new nuclear submarine last month.
Enemy aircraft bombed the submarine base at dawn.

definition: the act of formally giving a document or proposal for consideration

collocations.example: The submission date for proposals is next Friday.
We await the submission of your final report.

definition: dealing with real, important matters rather than small details

The two sides finally began substantive negotiations yesterday.

definition: a yellow chemical element that burns with a strong, unpleasant smell

Engineers measured the sulphur content in the crude oil.

definition: not thorough or deep; dealing only with the most obvious things

collocations.example: He has only a superficial knowledge of economics.
Their superficial analyzis missed the real problem entirely.

definition: a person who manages or supervises an organization or activity

collocations.example: The superintendent of schools announced the new calendar.

definition: to ride on waves towards the shore using a special board

collocations.example: He wants to learn to surf this summer.
The brothers love to surf the big waves.

definition: relating to surgery, the medical treatment that involves cutting the body

definition: the careful watching of a person or place, especially by police

A surveillance camera recorded the whole incident clearly.

definition: likely to be affected or harmed by a particular thing

collocations.example: Young children are susceptible to colds in winter.
The crops are highly susceptible to this common disease.

definition: an area of low, soft, wet land that is often covered by water

collocations.example: Birds nest among the trees in the mangrove swamp.
Workers drained the swamp to build the new road.

definition: to give something to someone and receive something else in return

collocations.example: Can we swap places so I can see better?

definition: to influence someone's opinion or make them change a decision

collocations.example: The speech did little to sway public opinion.
Advertisers try hard to sway voters before the election.

definition: a warm knitted piece of clothing worn on the upper body

collocations.example: He wore a thick wool sweater in the snow.
She bought a hand-knitted sweater at the market.

definition: to move around quickly in a circular, twisting pattern

definition: the quality of having balanced, matching parts on opposite sides

Many animals have bilateral symmetry in their bodies.

definition: a long piece of music written for a full orchestra to perform

The composer wrote his first symphony at twenty.

definition: made artificially from chemicals rather than from natural materials

collocations.example: These boots are made from durable synthetic materials.
Car tires are often made of synthetic rubber.

definition: a small, solid piece of medicine that you swallow

The doctor prescribed a chewable tablet for the children.

definition: a popular newspaper with short, sensational stories and many pictures

collocations.example: The tabloid newspaper printed the scandal on its front page.
A shocking tabloid headline grabbed everyone's attention today.

definition: a particular way of dealing with a situation or problem

collocations.example: Let's try a different tack to solve this problem.
The manager decided to change tack completely.

definition: a person whose job is to make or repair clothes

collocations.example: He took his suit to the tailor for alterations.
A skilled tailor made her wedding dress by hand.

definition: (of an animal) not wild and not afraid of people

collocations.example: The deer in the park are remarkably tame.
They kept a tame rabbit as a family pet.

definition: the brown color that the skin turns after time in the sun

collocations.example: She got a lovely golden tan on holiday.
He came back from the beach with a deep tan.

definition: real and clear enough to be noticed or measured

collocations.example: The new policy produced tangible benefits for the workers.
There is no tangible evidence of any crime.

definition: a tax that a government charges on goods coming into a country

definition: a person skilled in the practical use of equipment or machines

collocations.example: The laboratory technician prepared the samples for testing.
A skilled technician repaired the broken printer quickly.

definition: a young person between thirteen and nineteen years old

collocations.example: As a teen, she dreamed of becoming a doctor.
He spent his teen years in a small town.

definition: an old system for sending messages over long distances using electrical signals

collocations.example: A new telegraph line connected the two distant cities.
Birds perched on the old wooden telegraph pole.

definition: a tendency to become angry quickly and easily

collocations.example: He lost his temper when the meeting was canceled.
She has a bad temper early in the morning.

definition: a person's typical nature, especially how they usually feel and behave

collocations.example: Her calm temperament makes her a good team leader.
The actor was famous for his artistic temperament.

definition: relating to time or to the order in which things happen

The film plays with the temporal dimension of memory.

definition: not definite or final; still able to be changed

collocations.example: We made a tentative plan to meet on Friday.

definition: the period during which someone holds an important job or position

collocations.example: During his tenure as mayor, crime fell sharply.
She achieved a great deal in her short tenure.

definition: an area of land, especially when thinking about its physical features

collocations.example: The jeep handled the rough terrain with ease.
The soldiers trained in the harsh mountainous terrain.

definition: extremely good; excellent or wonderful

collocations.example: You did a terrific job on the presentation.
She looks terrific in her new blue dress.

definition: to make a formal statement of what is true in a court of law

collocations.example: The witness agreed to testify in court tomorrow.
She refused to testify against her own brother.

definition: relating to the study of religion and religious belief

collocations.example: He studied at a famous theological college abroad.
The scholars held a long theological debate yesterday.

definition: helping to cure illness or to improve a person's health

definition: after that particular time or event

definition: relating to or caused by heat

Firefighters used thermal imaging to find the survivors.

definition: the position and power of a king or queen

collocations.example: The young prince is the heir to the throne.
She will take the throne after her father dies.

definition: a dull, heavy sound made by a blow or a falling object

collocations.example: We heard a loud thump from the room upstairs.
We heard the thump of heavy footsteps on the stairs.

definition: arranged neatly, with everything in its proper place

collocations.example: He always works best at a clean, tidy desk.
Please keep your room tidy at all times.

definition: done for appearance only; small or nominal rather than genuine or substantial

collocations.example: They charge only a token fee for entry.
The small gift was a token gesture of thanks.

definition: the willingness to accept opinions or behavior you may not agree with

definition: willing to accept opinions or behavior different from your own

collocations.example: We should be tolerant of different points of view.
He stayed remarkably tolerant despite the constant noise.

definition: the number of people killed or harmed in an event

collocations.example: The death toll from the flood reached two hundred.
Officials feared the rising toll of the disaster.

definition: a large grave, especially one built of stone above the ground

collocations.example: Archaeologists discovered an ancient tomb beneath the temple.
Many tourists visit the tomb of the king.

definition: a small electric light that you carry in your hand

collocations.example: She shone a torch into the dark cellar.
He carried an electric torch during the power cut.

definition: great mental or physical suffering

collocations.example: She suffered years of mental torment after the accident.
He lay in torment, unable to sleep at night.

definition: to pull a vehicle or boat along using a rope or chain

collocations.example: The police will tow away illegally parked cars.
His powerful truck can tow a heavy trailer easily.

definition: a large area of land

collocations.example: They bought a large tract of land for farming.
A vast tract of forest was cleared for development.

definition: a powerful vehicle used on farms to pull heavy equipment

collocations.example: The farmer drove his tractor across the muddy field.
A farm tractor pulled the heavy plow slowly.

definition: a container on wheels that is pulled behind a vehicle

collocations.example: They attached the trailer to the back of the truck.
He loaded all the furniture onto a small trailer.

definition: calm, quiet, and peaceful

collocations.example: The inn has a tranquil atmosphere by the lake.
They led a tranquil life in the quiet countryside.

definition: to go beyond the usual limits of something

collocations.example: Great art can transcend cultural and language boundaries.
Her talent seemed to transcend all normal limitations.

definition: the process of moving people or goods from one place to another

collocations.example: Several items were damaged while in transit.
The city invested heavily in its mass transit system.

definition: allowing light through so that objects behind can be seen clearly

collocations.example: The box was made of clear transparent plastic.
The insect's delicate wings are almost transparent.

definition: to put your foot down while walking or stepping

collocations.example: You should tread carefully on the icy path.
Be careful not to tread on the flowers.

definition: a long, narrow hole dug in the ground

collocations.example: Workers dug a trench to lay the new pipes.
Soldiers sheltered in a deep trench during the battle.

definition: to flow slowly in a thin stream or in drops

collocations.example: Water trickled down the wall after the heavy rain.

definition: a group of three people or things, especially three musicians

definition: to become, or to make something, three times as large

collocations.example: The town's population tripled in size over a decade.
They had to triple the amount of staff.

definition: of little importance or value

collocations.example: It's a trivial matter not worth arguing about.
The problem may seem trivial, but it really isn't.

definition: a speed of movement between walking and running, especially of a horse

collocations.example: The horse broke into a trot across the field.
She crossed the yard at a brisk trot.

definition: a common freshwater fish that people catch and eat

collocations.example: We caught several rainbow trout in the river.
The restaurant serves fresh trout with lemon and herbs.

definition: a brass musical instrument that you play by blowing into it

collocations.example: He learned to play the trumpet at school.
The jazz band opened with a brilliant trumpet solo.

definition: a large container that you fill with water and sit in to wash

collocations.example: She loves to lie in the tub after work.
He filled the tub with warm, soapy water.

definition: sudden, violent movement of air, especially affecting an aircraft

definition: a surface layer of grass and the soil held together by its roots

collocations.example: The stadium installed new artificial turf last summer.
Workers laid fresh turf across the garden lawn.

definition: a slow-moving reptile with a hard shell, living on land or in water

collocations.example: A giant sea turtle swam past the divers.
The hard turtle shell protects it from predators.

definition: a sudden, small, uncontrolled movement of a muscle

collocations.example: He has a nervous twitch when he is tired.

definition: to write something using a keyboard on a computer or typewriter

collocations.example: She typed up the report before the morning meeting.
He carefully typed a letter to the manager.

definition: a painful, sore area on the skin or inside the body

collocations.example: The doctor said he had a stomach ulcer.

definition: a device you hold over your head to keep off rain

collocations.example: She opened her umbrella as the rain started.
They huddled under one umbrella in the pouring rain.

definition: agreed by everyone involved, with no one disagreeing

collocations.example: The committee reached a unanimous decision very quickly.
The new proposal passed by a unanimous vote.

definition: to think that something is smaller or less important than it really is

collocations.example: Never underestimate the difficulty of learning a new language.

definition: a university student who has not yet earned a first degree

collocations.example: She is an undergraduate student studying biology.

definition: to show that something is especially important

The manager underlined the point with a clear example.

definition: to support or maintain a law, decision, or principle

collocations.example: Police officers have a duty to uphold the law.

definition: standing straight up; vertical

collocations.example: She sat upright in her chair during the interview.
Please keep the heavy box in an upright position.

definition: the yellowish liquid waste that passes out of the body

definition: the amount that something is used, or the way it is used

definition: a person who shows people to their seats at an event

definition: completely; totally

definition: empty and available to be used or filled

collocations.example: The seat next to him was vacant all evening.

definition: a period of time spent away from work for rest or travel

collocations.example: They are on vacation in Hawaii this week.

definition: a substance given to protect people against a particular disease

Older people should get a flu vaccine each year.

definition: a space that is completely empty of air or other gas

definition: a device that controls the flow of liquid or gas through a pipe

collocations.example: The safety valve releases pressure from the boiler.

definition: a container used to hold cut flowers or for decoration

collocations.example: She arranged the roses in a tall glass vase.
A beautiful vase of flowers stood on the table.
